service_at_issue: Basic life support ground ambulance (A0429-RH) and mileage (A0425-RH) to hospital for nausea
outcome_note: The beneficiary was stable with no treatment needed, so other transport was not contraindicated; denial rests on section 1861(s)(7) and the beneficiary is liable.
facts: The attorney argues that the beneficiary’s daughter and the Benefits Counselor Coordinator (BCC) were not provided an opportunity to properly present their case.

Testimony presented during the hearing indicated that transport was in fact due to nausea; that the beneficiary’s caregiver would not have been able to transport her in her private vehicle; that the beneficiary was recently released from the hospital prior to transport. The medical records indicate that the beneficiary’s nausea was likely related to a recently prescribed medication and that the beneficiary was treated and released.
The appellant’s attorney provided additional argument in the form of a faxed affidavit. Exh. MAC-3.

In this case, the Patient Care Report (PCR) indicates that the beneficiary “stated she got up to use the restroom [that] morning and felt nauseated.” Exh. 3 at 8-12. Further, the PCR states that the EMT “assessed the patient and found no other symptoms.” Id. Nothing in the record reflects that the beneficiary required or was provided pain medications, oxygen, or any treatment during the evaluation or ambulance trip.
